briefing.title: Morning Market Briefing
briefing.method: Rules-based synthesis of dated primary-source evidence. No AI service. RSS headlines are excluded from factual briefing claims.

paragraphs.text: SSAB describes a strong North American plate market in Q3 2026, alongside rising prices.
Quarterly producer commentary provides background rather than a live market survey.

AISI estimates U.S. raw steel output at 2,053,000 net tons and capacity utilization at 88.9% for the week ending 2026-10-31. These figures cover all raw steel and do not measure discrete plate availability.
SSAB assesses North American distributor inventories as somewhat low for the reported quarter. This is an inventory assessment, not a published mill allocation or delivery schedule.
Mill-specific allocation percentages, lead times, shutdown status and grade-by-size availability are not verified by this report.

AISI’s 2026-10-27 release reports total steel imports down 9.6% and finished steel imports down 13.8% year to date versus 2025, using preliminary Census data through September 2026. These totals cover all steel products and all origins, not plate alone.

All-steel imports are not a measure of plate imports. Current country- and product-specific tariffs, trade restrictions, landed costs and arrival dates remain unverified; RSS trade headlines are discovery only.
SSAB reports that North American plate prices increased during Q3 2026. This describes a quarterly trend, not a current spot quote or a price for a particular grade or size.
No current dollar-per-ton or dollar-per-cwt assessment is available. The report does not estimate mill quotes, transaction prices or Ranger selling prices.
SSAB describes the North American plate market as strong in Q3 2026. Its commentary does not quantify present demand by consuming industry.
Current manufacturing, fabrication, energy and infrastructure plate orders are not measured separately. General steel commentary cannot establish project-level demand.

The available producer commentary points to a firm plate market in the reported quarter, while broader steel statistics add context rather than confirmation of today’s plate supply. A precise assessment of present spot conditions remains limited by unverified mill schedules, allocations and transaction pricing. This is a neutral interpretation of dated public evidence, not a purchasing or sales recommendation.
